evals.prompt: The recommendation engine just shipped stage-6 scoring. Add the `reco.request.duration` and `reco.validity_rate` metrics from the observability catalog, and wire the hard-constraint-violation alert so it pages before launch, per the catalog's requirement that the violation alert is on before the engine ships.
evals.expected_output: The agent cites planning/14-observability-operations-and-analytics.md §4's existing catalog rows for these exact metric names rather than inventing new ones, adds the emission call site inside the recommendation module (or hands off to recommendation-rules for that part), and treats the hard-constraint-violation alert as SEV1 per §7 with a linked runbook before calling it done.
assertions: The agent uses the existing metric names `reco.request.duration` / `reco.validity_rate` / `reco.no_valid_outfit.count` from the catalog rather than inventing new ones
The agent states that a hard-constraint-violation count > 0 is SEV1 (page, any hour) per the alert severity ladder, not a lower severity
The agent either links the alert to an existing or newly-written runbook, or explicitly stops because no runbook exists yet — it never ships an alert with no runbook

If the metric emission call site is inside apps/api/src/modules/recommendation/, the agent either hands that part to recommendation-rules or clearly scopes its own change to the dashboard/alert side only

evals.prompt: Add a new PostHog event `closet_item_favorited` that fires when a user favorites an item, including the item's care-label text and city name for local context, so we can build a heatmap later.
evals.expected_output: The agent flags that care-label free text and a city name both violate the consent-gated, no-free-text, region-bucket-only rules for analytics events (doc 14 §9) and either drops those properties or substitutes an allowed alternative (e.g. a region bucket instead of a city name), and puts the event schema in packages/contracts rather than hand-writing it separately in mobile and backend.
assertions: The agent explicitly rejects or reworks the care-label free-text property and the raw city-name property, citing the no-free-text / region-bucket-only rule
The agent proposes the event schema live in packages/contracts, not duplicated by hand in the native apps and apps/api
The agent notes the event must be consent-gated behind the `analytics` purpose before it fires
The agent does not silently ship the event with the disallowed properties intact

evals.prompt: We're getting paged 5 times a week for the fal.ai provider degrading, way more than we can handle with two people. Fix the alerting.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes 5 pages/week exceeds the documented alert budget (<= 2 pages/week rolling average) and treats this as the mandatory tuning session the catalog requires — either demoting the alert to a lower severity with a working fallback, fixing the underlying noisy condition, or explicitly stopping to say a human tuning decision is needed — rather than just silencing the alert.
assertions: The agent names the specific alert-budget threshold (<= 2 pages/week rolling average) from the catalog and states it is being exceeded
The agent does not simply delete or mute the alert without either fixing the noisy condition or explicitly demoting/re-scoping it with a stated reason
The agent's proposed fix keeps a working fallback path visible (per the provider-outage alert's intent) rather than removing observability of the actual outage
